steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Nebbiolo makes Barolo, Barbaresco and Roero: pale but powerful, with tar, roses and high tannin. Barbera, the most planted red, gives juicy, high-acid, low-tannin wines. Dolcetto gives soft, dark, early-drinking reds. Other reds include Freisa, Grignolino and Ruchè.

steps.title: Whites
steps.body: Moscato Bianco makes Asti and Moscato d'Asti, sweet and lightly sparkling. Arneis, revived in the Roero from the 1970s, gives fragrant, pear-scented whites. Cortese makes Gavi, crisp and mineral, in the south-east. Timorasso, near Tortona, is a rising white grape.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its wine.
steps.explanation: Each grape has its signature wine.

steps.body: Langhe Nebbiolo, a DOC, offers Nebbiolo's tar and roses at a much lower price than Barolo, and is ready to drink younger.

steps.prompt: Which is Piedmont's most planted red grape?
steps.explanation: Barbera covers the most area, though Nebbiolo is the most prestigious.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Nebbiolo, Barbera and Dolcetto lead the reds
Moscato, Arneis and Cortese lead the whites
Barbera is the most planted; Nebbiolo the most prestigious
